verdicts.note: Claude sits dead on the sprocket hub/axis center; codex is ~25px low-right of the hub.
The prominent brass part behind the green post is unmistakably the tapered fine-ringed cone stack (matches the side view); codex identified it correctly, claude wrongly called the cone occluded.

Claude marked an ambiguous brass gear at the cone's base/left that is most likely the cone base or crank-side gearing, not a confirmed helical cylinder gear; the two dedicated cylinder gears are largely hidden, so codex's occluded call is more defensible.
Claude's point lands squarely on the cone body (mislabeled); it is the cone, not a second cylinder gear, so codex's occluded is correct.
Claude is right on the top-outer corner of the left end-cap; codex is ~20px down-left of it.
This corner is over the front-right post junction; codex is nearer the top-outer corner while claude sits low on the front-bottom edge ~90px off — both imperfect.
Both are within ~18px of the top-right outer corner of the far green end-cap; claude marginally better at the top corner, codex slightly low.
Both correctly list it occluded (hidden behind the top casting from this front-right view).
Both land essentially on the front-left bottom corner of the base slab within ~10px.
Claude is within ~8px of the nearest (front-right) bottom corner; codex's point sits ~144px up the right-side face, not at the bottom corner.
Claude is ~13px from the back-right BOTTOM corner; codex marks the top edge near the post ~95px too high (base corners are bottom corners).
In this front-right view the back-left base corner is hidden; codex's point floats in black background off the slab, so claude's occluded is correct.
Both correctly report the rocker-arm fan as edge-on/occluded behind the central column in this view (claude listed all four corners, codex bundled them).

summary: Roughly balanced, with claude stronger on point placement and orientation reasoning, codex stronger on gear identification. Claude nailed the pinion and the base corners (front-left, front-right, back-right) and correctly read the view as showing the machine's FRONT + RIGHT side, whereas codex's prose said 'left side' (wrong) and it placed base_front_right and base_back_right off the true bottom corners and invented a base_back_left dot in empty black space. Conversely, the prominent tapered fine-ringed brass part is the CONE gear: codex identified it correctly and conservatively marked the (occluded) cylinder gears, while claude wrongly split the cone into two 'cylinder gears' and declared the cone occluded. Systematic notes: codex tends to place slab corners up the visible side face rather than at the true bottom corner; claude tends to over-claim visibility of the base gears.
